name: CEAVOX
summary: I engineered event workflows that connect registration, voting, ticketing, payments and organiser operations.
desc: A multi-module events platform for elections, award voting and ticketed experiences, with connected participant, organiser and administrative workflows.
label: Voting / Elections / Ticketing
challenge: An event is not just a page or checkout button. Registration, eligibility, payment status, voting, ticket delivery, check-in and organiser balances have to connect across several user roles and event formats.
contribution: Full-stack engineering across React/TypeScript interfaces and a Convex backend: event configuration, participation flows, payment integrations, webhook handling, transactional email, ticketing, organiser tools and finance-facing workflows.
decisions: One platform, different event engines
Built distinct experiences for elections, award voting and ticketing while sharing event setup, public discovery and organiser tooling.
Money needs its own lifecycle
Connected payment initiation, callback and webhook paths with transaction records, verification and reconciliation logic rather than treating payment as a visual success screen.
From purchase to gate check-in
Linked ticket issuance, QR/reference lookup and attendance workflows so ticket status can be checked against backend event records.
Tools for the people running events
Implemented organiser-facing configuration, participant management, transaction views and operational actions alongside the public participant experience.
journeys: Organiser configures and publishes an event
Participant registers, votes or obtains a ticket
Platform processes results, payments and notifications
Organiser manages attendance and financial activity
outcome: An operating events platform with interconnected public experiences and substantial internal systems. This case study illustrates engineering scope; individual production workflows remain subject to ongoing verification and improvement.

implementation.heading: Frontend & event experiences
items: React/TypeScript event discovery, event pages and organiser-facing dashboards.
Event creation and configuration interfaces spanning elections, award voting and ticketed events.
Contestant, voter and attendee registration flows, moderation interfaces and result views.

implementation.heading: Backend, integrations & automation
items: Convex queries, mutations and actions connecting event state, participation records and role-aware workflows.
Payment-gateway integrations including Paystack and Flutterwave-related flows; webhook verification and reconciliation pathways.
Resend-powered transactional email workflows, QR-coded e-ticket issuance and backend-driven gate validation.

implementation.heading: Operations & financial systems
items: Transaction history, export and financial visibility for organisers and system administrators.
Commission, balance, withdrawal and payout-request workflows, with finance states handled separately from public UI.
Automated jobs, approval flows, test coverage and production-oriented error and retry handling across connected features.

name: HearIntel
summary: I built clinical workflows and data systems spanning audiology patient management and registry operations.
desc: A full-stack audiology platform comprising a clinical patient-management system and a separately governed hearing-health registry.
label: Clinical software / Registry
challenge: Clinical software must support detailed patient encounters while keeping facilities, staff responsibilities and registry reporting separate. The difficult part is modelling those workflows and access boundaries across UI, API and database.
contribution: Full-stack work across React interfaces, backend APIs and PostgreSQL/Supabase data services, including patient and facility workflows, clinical assessment modules, permissions, reporting surfaces and deployment.
decisions: Two products, two responsibilities
Separated clinic-level patient operations from national/state-level registry reporting so the interface and data access follow different purposes.
Clinical detail without UI chaos
Developed structured audiology assessment and management experiences that move across several clinical modules and patient encounters.
Facility- and role-aware access
Implemented interfaces and supporting access flows for clinic staff, administrators and authorised users across distinct organisational contexts.
Operational continuity
Connected appointment, worklist, records and reporting surfaces with supporting APIs, deployment environments and backend checks.
journeys: Facility or authorised staff member signs in
Clinician works through an audiology encounter
Records, assessments and reports remain in the appropriate clinical workspace
Authorised registry users access their distinct reporting workflows
outcome: A live healthcare software project with rich clinical and operational functionality. Registry analytics and some sensitive clinical workflows are still undergoing governance and production-readiness work; no patient information is displayed in this portfolio.

implementation.heading: Clinical product engineering
items: Patient registration, clinical worklists, appointments, longitudinal records and visit-management interfaces.
Audiology-specific assessments including otoscopy, pure-tone audiometry, speech and immittance-related workflows.
Clinical conclusions, hearing-care documentation, reports and record navigation across patient encounters.

implementation.heading: Backend & data systems
items: React frontend integration with backend API services hosted on Render and PostgreSQL services through Supabase.
Facility onboarding, staff roles, tenant-aware access paths and private patient-data handling mechanisms.
Shared underlying data concepts with separately governed PMS and registry responsibilities.

implementation.heading: Registry, quality & deployment
items: Registry onboarding, facility and administration interfaces plus regional hearing-health reporting foundations.
Audit-oriented workflows, review states and privacy-conscious approaches to patient-derived reporting.
Frontend deployment on Vercel, backend deployment on Render and automated UI/backend verification efforts.

name: QPrep
summary: I developed a study-resource platform with accounts, academic metadata, file storage and moderation workflows.
desc: An academic past-question repository with student access, structured course materials, file-management workflows and administrative tools.
label: Education / Academic resources
challenge: A useful past-question repository needs more than PDF links. Students need relevant course material; uploads need consistent metadata; and moderators need a process to review resources before publication.
contribution: Full-stack development spanning public account screens, student resource views, administrative interfaces, Convex data functions, file storage, course metadata and upload-review flows.
decisions: Organise around real academic context
Structured papers around institution, department, level, course, semester and session details so materials can be presented in a useful academic context.
Separate raw uploads from published material
Modelled a review queue for newly uploaded PDFs and a distinct published-material catalogue instead of publishing every upload immediately.
Build tooling for academic administrators
Developed student-facing screens alongside management views for reviewing, creating and removing course materials.
Connect the files to the data
Used generated upload URLs and storage identifiers to associate uploaded files with searchable academic records.
journeys: Contributor or staff user submits a resource
Moderator reviews and publishes material to the catalogue
outcome: A live academic resource project with substantial data and upload-management code behind the public registration screens. Some administrative and permission paths require continued hardening; no unverified user-growth metrics are claimed.

implementation.heading: Backend & file management
items: Convex queries and mutations for paper records, metadata, retrieval and file references.
Generated upload URLs and stored document identifiers for PDF/resource uploads.
Bulk and multi-department material publishing paths with course and semester classification.

implementation.heading: Moderation & administration
items: Raw-upload review queues and pending-material management interfaces.
Administrator publishing, deletion and catalogue-management functionality.
Role concepts for students, moderators and super-admins, with academic scopes represented in the data model.

name: Safe Nest
summary: I built rental-platform interfaces across tenant journeys, landlord operations and connected payments.
desc: A multi-role property-rental frontend for tenants and landlords, integrated with a separately maintained backend API.
label: Housing / Web experience
challenge: A rental platform has long, stateful journeys: discovering homes, applying, reviewing applications and paying. Each role needs a clear experience that handles real API responses, loading states and failures.
contribution: Frontend engineering for a React-based property platform: responsive tenant and landlord flows, API integration, authentication screens, rental applications, payment UI and reusable dashboard components. The backend was maintained separately.
decisions: Different interfaces for different roles
Built role-specific React routes and dashboards for tenants and landlords instead of forcing every task into one generic interface.
Applications are guided journeys
Implemented multi-step interfaces for rental applications and property creation/editing, including validation, progress and status feedback.
Make external APIs usable
Connected Axios-based client services and defensive response handling to a backend maintained by another developer.
Payments need clear states
Built frontend payment initiation, callback and status interfaces around backend-controlled Flutterwave flows.
journeys: Tenant applies and follows application status
Payment screens connect to the existing backend's payment flow
outcome: A multifaceted rental frontend with live API-connected tenant and landlord flows. Backend ownership belongs to another developer; certain admin, messaging and analytics screens remain prototypes rather than completed services.

implementation.heading: Tenant experience
items: Property discovery, listing details and application interfaces, including multi-step form handling.
Tenant dashboards, application-status screens and transaction/payment views.
Responsive layouts, loading skeletons, error feedback and reusable property components.

implementation.heading: Landlord experience
items: Landlord dashboard and property listing/management UI connected to the separate backend API.
Add/edit property wizard and application review/accept-or-decline interfaces.
Client-side filtering, confirmation modals and status-driven property cards.

implementation.heading: Frontend architecture & integrations
items: React Router role-specific journeys, shared layouts and session-aware protected routes.
Axios integration, response-shape normalization and service/hook patterns for asynchronous data.
Flutterwave-related payment UI, checkout redirects and callback/status handling in the frontend.
